claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys have a vast multi-principal-element compositional space.
RHEAs have diverse microstructures that are mostly BCC solid solutions with severe lattice distortion.
A machine-learning framework trained on integrated thermo-kinetic, simulation, and experimental data can rapidly identify promising RHEA compositions.
Machine-learning-designed RHEAs can simultaneously improve intrinsic strength and ductility and reduce weight relative to traditionally designed alloys.
Historical thermo-kinetic, simulation, and experimental datasets can be used to predict intrinsic strength, ductility, and weight.
Ambient and elevated temperatures are relevant testing conditions for the intended high-performance alloy applications.
The computational screening will be followed by experimental validation.
Microstructural features such as lattice distortion and phase stability correlate with mechanical performance in RHEAs.
A machine-learning model can extract complex composition-performance relationships from multi-fidelity datasets.
Data-driven modeling can rapidly narrow a large compositional space to a small set of candidate alloys.
Selected RHEA compositions will have significantly higher intrinsic strength than alloys identified using conventional thermo-kinetic and simulation methods.
Selected RHEA compositions will have significantly higher ductility than alloys identified using conventional thermo-kinetic and simulation methods.
Selected RHEA compositions will have lower density than alloys identified using conventional thermo-kinetic and simulation methods.
Traditional exhaustive thermo-kinetic analysis and high-throughput simulation require extensive computational resources and time.
The proposed approach will be most effective in well-sampled regions of composition space.
Predictions for extreme or sparsely represented compositions will be more uncertain.
Incomplete or low-quality datasets can limit prediction accuracy.
Model extrapolation into underrepresented compositional regimes can limit prediction accuracy.
